concepts.title: Recognising similarity
concepts.explanation: AA compares two angles, SAS compares two proportional sides and the included angle, and SSS compares all three side ratios. Always match corresponding vertices.

example.problem: Two triangles have sides 2, 4 and 6, 12, with equal included angles of 50°. Which criterion applies?
steps: Both side ratios are 1:3 and the included angles agree.

concepts.commonMistake: Two sides and a non-included angle do not establish SAS similarity.

concepts.title: Corresponding sides and scale
concepts.explanation: In similar triangles all corresponding lengths have the same scale factor. Their perimeters have this factor too.

example.problem: Similar triangles have smaller:larger side ratio 3:5. A larger side is 10 cm. Find its smaller match in cm.

concepts.commonMistake: Keep smaller-to-larger or larger-to-smaller ratios consistent.
checklist: Apply it to the required length.

concepts.title: Basic proportionality theorem
concepts.explanation: If DE is parallel to BC in triangle ABC, with D on AB and E on AC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. Conversely equal ratios with points on those sides establish parallelism.

example.problem: In triangle ABC, DE ∥ BC, D on AB, E on AC. DB = 6, AE = 4, EC = 6 cm. Find AD in cm.

concepts.commonMistake: Do not mix a part-to-part ratio with a part-to-whole ratio.

concepts.title: Using three side ratios
concepts.explanation: SSS similarity requires one common ratio for all three corresponding sides. Sorting sides by length can help find the correspondence.

example.problem: Similar triangles have ordered side lists (5, 12, 13) and (10, x, 26). Find x.
steps: The first and third side ratios both give scale 2.

concepts.commonMistake: Matching just one or two side ratios is insufficient for SSS.

concepts.title: Similar subtriangles
concepts.explanation: When DE is parallel to BC, triangles ADE and ABC are similar. Therefore AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC. Whole sides include both component segments.

example.problem: In triangle ABC, DE ∥ BC, D on AB, E on AC. AD = 4, AE = 6, AC = 18 cm. Find AB in cm.

concepts.commonMistake: AB is AD + DB, not DB alone.
checklist: Add or subtract segments only after solving.

questions.prompt: Two triangles each have angles 40° and 40°. Which criterion proves similarity?
questions.explanation: Two corresponding angles agree; the third agrees because each angle sum is 180°.

questions.prompt: Two triangles each have angles 60° and 40°. Which criterion proves similarity?
questions.explanation: Two corresponding angles agree; the third agrees because each angle sum is 180°.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have smaller:larger side ratio 2:3. A smaller side is 4 cm. Find its larger match in cm.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 3/2: 4 × 3/2 = 6.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have smaller:larger side ratio 2:3. A smaller side is 6 cm. Find its larger match in cm.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 3/2: 6 × 3/2 = 9.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have smaller:larger side ratio 3:5. A larger side is 20 cm. Find its smaller match in cm.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have perimeters 24 and 36 cm. A side in the first is 4 cm. Find the corresponding side in the second in cm.
questions.explanation: Perimeters and corresponding sides have the same ratio 2:3. The side is 4 × 3/2 = 6.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have perimeters 36 and 54 cm. A side in the first is 6 cm. Find the corresponding side in the second in cm.
questions.explanation: Perimeters and corresponding sides have the same ratio 2:3. The side is 6 × 3/2 = 9.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have perimeters 48 and 72 cm. A side in the first is 8 cm. Find the corresponding side in the second in cm.
questions.explanation: Perimeters and corresponding sides have the same ratio 2:3. The side is 8 × 3/2 = 12.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D is on AB, E on AC, DE ∥ BC. AD = 2, DB = 4, AE = 2 cm. Find EC in cm.
questions.explanation: AD/DB = AE/EC gives 2/4 = 2/EC. EC = 4.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D is on AB, E on AC, DE ∥ BC. AD = 3, DB = 6, AE = 3 cm. Find EC in cm.
questions.explanation: AD/DB = AE/EC gives 3/6 = 3/EC. EC = 6.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D is on AB, E on AC, DE ∥ BC. AD = 4, DB = 8, AE = 4 cm. Find EC in cm.
questions.explanation: AD/DB = AE/EC gives 4/8 = 4/EC. EC = 8.

questions.explanation: AD/DB = 1/2, so DB = 24. AB = AD + DB = 36.

questions.prompt: A triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 cm is similar to one with corresponding sides 6, 8, x cm. Find x.
questions.explanation: The common scale factor is 2; x = 5 × 2 = 10.

questions.prompt: A triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 cm is similar to one with corresponding sides 9, 12, x cm. Find x.

questions.prompt: A triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 cm is similar to one with corresponding sides 12, 16, x cm. Find x.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have ordered side lists (5, 12, 13) and (10, x, 26). Find x.
questions.explanation: The first and third side ratios both give scale 2. The middle side is 12 × 2 = 24.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have ordered side lists (5, 12, 13) and (15, x, 39). Find x.
questions.explanation: The first and third side ratios both give scale 3. The middle side is 12 × 3 = 36.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles have ordered side lists (5, 12, 13) and (20, x, 52). Find x.

questions.prompt: A triangle similar to one with sides 5, 12, 13 cm has perimeter 60 cm. Find its shortest side in cm.
questions.explanation: The original perimeter is 30, so scale = 2. The shortest side is 10.

questions.prompt: A triangle similar to one with sides 5, 12, 13 cm has perimeter 90 cm. Find its shortest side in cm.
